page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n4a server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an ARMv8 Neoverse-N3 processor running at 3.4 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core, 8.0 GB of system memory providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and no local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs. The CPU architecture is arm64, equipped with a cache hierarchy consisting of 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 112 MB L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography enabled.

Benchmark data reveals a mix of performance characteristics. The server demonstrates strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression, reaching 32.69 GB/sec. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is average at 2058.78, and bzip3 single-threaded decompression is also average at 9.4 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show limitations. Multi-core CPU performance is weak at 4086.82, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor at 18.69 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks is poor at 141.61 GB/sec, while large block read-only bandwidth is weak at 36.91 GB/sec, though large block write bandwidth remains average at 36.72 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput is weak at 5.09 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4a-standard-2 offers an entry-level ARM-based resource profile with dedicated physical cores, avoiding the CPU credit limitations of burstable instances while maintaining a low resource footprint. Given the lack of local storage and GPUs, combined with weak multi-core and memory bandwidth performance, this server is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, development environments, or simple background utility tasks that do not require high memory throughput or parallel processing.
